title: Why Dreamcast’s 1 GB GD‑ROM Was a Game‑Changer

scenes.text: The 1999 Dreamcast used a 1 GB GD‑ROM, 40% larger than a standard CD
A GD‑ROM could hold up to 1 GB of data, compared to the 700 MB limit of CD‑ROMs
Sega marketed the extra space for full‑motion video and richer textures in games like Shenmue
Despite the advantage, the GD‑ROM was dropped because manufacturing costs were too high, not because of low sales
Follow to stay ahead of the tech curve.

description: Dreamcast’s 1 GB GD‑ROM promised bigger games, but high production costs sealed its fate. Learn the hidden economics behind the console’s bold move. Follow for more retro tech!
